app.name: Rikuri Node
cert.title: Let’s make this connection private
cert.lead: Your node made its own certificate. Install it once on this device, and no one else on your network can read what you type here, like your password.
cert.installed_text: Continue on the private page. There you’ll check that it’s really your node before you type anything.
cert.stop: Not sure? You can stop here. Nothing on your node changes until you claim it.
steps.iphone.1: Tap Download the certificate, then Allow.
steps.iphone.2: Open Settings, tap Profile Downloaded, then Install.
steps.iphone.3: Go to Settings › General › About › Certificate Trust Settings and turn on Rikuri Node CA.
steps.android.2: Open Settings and search for “CA certificate”. Tap it, then Install anyway.
steps.android.3: Choose rikuri-node-ca.crt from your downloads. The menus’ names differ a little from phone to phone.
steps.mac.1: Click Download the certificate, then open rikuri-node-ca.crt from Downloads. Keychain Access opens.
steps.mac.2: Double-click Rikuri Node CA, open Trust, and set “When using this certificate” to Always Trust.
steps.mac.3: Close the window, and enter your Mac’s password to confirm.
steps.windows.1: Click Download the certificate, then open rikuri-node-ca.crt and choose Install Certificate.
steps.windows.2: Choose Current User, then “Place all certificates in the following store”, and pick Trusted Root Certification Authorities.
steps.windows.3: Click Finish, then Yes when Windows asks whether to install it.
steps.linux.2: In Firefox: Settings › Privacy & Security › Certificates › View Certificates › Authorities › Import, and tick “Trust this CA to identify websites”.
steps.linux.3: In Chrome or Chromium: Settings › Privacy and security › Security › Manage certificates › Authorities › Import.
secure.title: The connection is private
secure.lead: Your browser now trusts your node’s certificate. One last check makes sure it’s really your node, and not something pretending to be it.
secure.check1_after: . Its screen shows a fingerprint: two lines of letters and numbers.
secure.check2: Here, click the padlock beside the address, then the certificate, and find its SHA-256 fingerprint.
secure.check3: They must match exactly. If they don’t, stop, and unplug the node’s network cable.
secure.why: Why your browser and not this page? A page can be copied by anyone. Only your browser knows which certificate it is really talking to.
secure.next: Next you’ll claim the node with the code on its screen, and choose your password. That comes with the next update.
state.expired: The code on the node’s screen has expired. Press Enter at the node for a new one.
state.retired: Too many wrong codes. Press Enter at the node for a new one.
state.unarmed: No code yet. Press Enter at the node’s claim screen for one.
state.unknown: Couldn’t read the node’s setup state. Reload the page to try again.
